summary: MOONTRIP is a bilingual (ES/EN) tactical web simulator that trains young explorers as Quarantine and Life Support (ECLSS) Officers inside an Artemis lunar base airlock at the Shackleton Crater. It addresses the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by translating real NASA-STD-3001 and NASA BVAD parameters into hands-on mechanics where players balance four critical subsystems:Oxygen, Radiation Shielding, Nuclear Power (Kilopower), and Hydroponic Biomass (APH). Connected live to the NASA DONKI and NASA NeoWs APIs, real-time solar flares and near-Earth asteroids dynamically alter station radiation and power while players inspect arrivals using dual-spectrum X-Ray/UV scanners and perform first-person EVA repairs. This project is vital because it bridges complex aerospace telemetry and accessible STEM education: built on a zero-external-asset procedural architecture (code-driven SVG and Web Audio API), it runs instantly in any classroom browser worldwide without heavy downloads.
details: This web-based video game serves as a simulator for a civilization on the Moon, with resource availability determined by the selected difficulty level. It is designed for children aged 7 to 12, offering them an engaging way to explore space while developing problem-solving skills through decision-making. The game includes storage facilities for crops, energy, and oxygen, as well as protection against radiation. Additionally, an English-language option is available. The project allows children to interact with data while having fun. It was built using JavaScript (JS), HTML, and CSS, with DeepSeek and Antigravity utilized as supporting tools. This creative project incorporates NASA data into a decision-making system, where children can level up by making the best possible choices. Our team focused on fostering an interest in space among children, while helping them understand how their decisions can lead to positive outcomes.
